parsed.why: The national border, passport and custody risks apply, and national facilities restrictions reach the capital directly. No additional local ban is documented; its comparatively favorable local profile is fragile because national authorities can override it.

A statewide rule bars trans visitors from public multi-occupancy facilities, a continuous exposure, alongside thin state-level recourse and hostile policy signals. National entry and document risks add to this, though no local enforcement case is documented.

A recent mob assault over restroom use brought charges against victims, no attacker arrest, hospital denial and men's-jail placement despite female ID. This state-tolerated exposure and weak recourse compound the national restrictions; the violence-rate figures are unusable.

Operating state protections include facilities access, anti-discrimination enforcement, refuge measures and court-ordered care, materially mitigating the shared national risks. National border and custody exposures remain; funding pressure and pending ballot measures make protection less secure.

The state order defines sex at birth and backs segregated facilities; a documented trans woman was assaulted in men's custody, with courts dismissing her claims. These hostile institutional signals compound national exposure, despite some national protections.
